provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Phonics: digraphs sh and ch
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify words with sh and ch sounds.
The pupils should be able to sort words with sh and ch sounds.
Introduction:
We have learned single letter sounds. Today we learn two letters making one sound.
Content:
Digraphs are two letters making one sound. Sh sound is in words like ship and shop. Ch sound is in words like chat and chip. Let us practice these sounds together. We can find these sounds in many Nigerian words.
Class activity:
Sort word cards with sh and ch sounds into two groups.
Evaluation questions:
Circle the sh words. Circle the ch words. Make a sentence with a sh word.
Summary:
We can now identify and sort words with sh and ch sounds.

topics.title: Comprehension: the market
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read the market passage.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about the market.
Introduction:
We all know what a market looks like. Today we read about a market.
Content:
Read the passage about the market. It tells us about things sold at the market. We see people buying and selling. We hear noise and see many colours. After reading, we will answer questions about what we read.
Class activity:
Read the passage in groups. Answer the questions together.
Evaluation questions:
What is sold at the market? Who buys things at the market? What do you see at the market?
Summary:
We can read and understand a passage about the market.

topics.title: Grammar: describing words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify adjectives for size and colour.
The pupils should be able to use adjectives to describe objects.
Introduction:
We use words to describe things. Some words tell how big or what colour.
Content:
Adjectives are describing words. Size adjectives tell how big or small. Examples are big, small, tall, short. Colour adjectives tell the colour. Examples are red, blue, green, yellow. We can use these words to describe objects like a big bag or a red dress.
Class activity:
Describe objects in the classroom using size and colour words.
Evaluation questions:
Name three size adjectives. Name three colour adjectives. Describe a naira note.
Summary:
We can use adjectives to describe how things look.

topics.title: Grammar: is, am, are
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use is, am, are correctly in sentences.
The pupils should be able to fill gaps with is, am, are.
Introduction:
We use special words to show who is doing something. These words are is, am, are.
Content:
Is is used with he, she, it. Am is used with I. Are is used with you, we, they. For example, He is tall. I am happy. They are friends. We must use the right word with each subject.
Class activity:
Fill in the blanks with is, am, are in sentences about our classroom.
Evaluation questions:
Complete the sentences: I ___ happy. She ___ tall. They ___ friends.
Summary:
We can use is, am, are correctly in sentences.

topics.title: Vocabulary: opposites
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify opposite words.
The pupils should be able to use opposites in sentences.
Introduction:
Some words are opposites. They have opposite meanings.
Content:
Opposites are words with opposite meanings. Big and small are opposites. Hot and cold are opposites. Happy and sad are opposites. We can use these words to compare things. For example, The bag is big but the shoe is small.
Class activity:
Match opposite word cards and make sentences with them.
Evaluation questions:
Name three pairs of opposites. Use big and small in a sentence. What is the opposite of hot?
Summary:
We can identify and use opposite words.

topics.title: Composition: my best friend
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write about their best friend in four lines.
The pupils should be able to edit and read their composition.
Introduction:
We all have friends. Today we write about our best friend.
Content:
A composition is a piece of writing. We will write four lines about our best friend. We can write about their name, what they like, and why they are our friend. After writing, we will check for mistakes and read it aloud.
Class activity:
Write four lines about your best friend. Exchange with a partner to check.
Evaluation questions:
What is the name of your best friend? What does your best friend like to do? Why is your friend special?
Summary:
We can write and edit a short composition about our best friend.

topics.title: Story time and retelling
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to listen to a story.
The pupils should be able to retell a story in their own words.
Introduction:
Stories are fun to listen to. Today we will listen to a story and then tell it ourselves.
Content:
First, we will listen to a story about a clever rabbit. The story shows how the rabbit outsmarted a big animal. After listening, we will retell the story in our own words. We must remember the main points in order.
Class activity:
Retell the story in groups. Each person says one sentence.
Evaluation questions:
What was the story about? Who was clever in the story? What happened at the end of the story?
Summary:
We can listen to a story and retell it in our own words.

topics.title: Handwriting and dictation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to practice joined writing.
The pupils should be able to write a sentence from dictation.
Introduction:
Good handwriting is important. Today we practice writing letters together and writing sentences.
Content:
Joined writing is when letters in a word are connected. We practice joining letters like a and b. Then the teacher will say a sentence slowly and we will write it down. We must listen carefully and write the words correctly.
Class activity:
Practice joining letters on paper. Then write a dictated sentence.
Evaluation questions:
Why is good handwriting important? How do we join letters in writing? Write this sentence: My dog is big.
Summary:
We can practice joined writing and write from dictation.

topics.title: Punctuation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use capital letters and full stops.
The pupils should be able to use question marks.
Introduction:
We use marks to show how sentences should be read. These are called punctuation marks.
Content:
Capital letters start sentences and names. Full stops end sentences. Question marks go at the end of questions. For example, Abuja is the capital of Nigeria. Do you like rice? We must use these marks correctly when we write.
Class activity:
Add capital letters, full stops and question marks to sentences.
Evaluation questions:
When do we use capital letters? When do we use full stops? When do we use question marks?
Summary:
We can use punctuation marks correctly in our writing.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to review term work.
The pupils should be able to participate in a class quiz.
Introduction:
Today we revise what we learned this term and have a fun quiz.
Content:
We will go through all the topics we learned this term. Phonics, comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, composition, and punctuation. Then we will have a quiz with questions from all these topics. This will help us remember what we learned.
Class activity:
Play a quiz game in teams. Answer questions about term work.
Evaluation questions:
What are digraphs? Name an adjective. When do we use full stops?
Summary:
We have reviewed what we learned this term and can answer questions about it.
